Drive: Motor overtemperature
meaning: The S210 calculated or measured that the motor is hotter than its limit.
symptoms: Trips after the axis has worked hard for a while, or straight away if the temperature signal is lost.
causes: Motor overloaded; ambient temperature too high; motor mounted where heat can't escape; temperature signal lost through a damaged OCC cable or encoder.
checks: Feel whether the motor is really hot; check the load and duty cycle; inspect the OCC cable and its connector at the motor.
repairable: Yes: encoder, bearing and winding repairs on 1FK2 motors are common.

Drive: Commutation angle incorrect (motor model)
meaning: The S210 found that the motor's magnetic position doesn't match what the encoder reports (wrong commutation angle).
symptoms: The motor runs rough, jumps or runs away on enable, or trips straight after starting.
causes: Motor phases swapped; encoder knocked out of alignment or damaged; encoder speed signal disturbed; wrong motor data or unstable control settings.
checks: Check the motor phase order at the converter; check whether the motor was recently repaired or the encoder replaced; inspect the OCC cable.
repairable: Yes: encoder replacement and alignment is a standard servo motor repair.

Drive: Motor encoder not ready
meaning: The motor encoder told the S210 it isn't ready, so the converter can't control the motor.
symptoms: The axis won't enable; often appears together with other encoder messages.
causes: Encoder failed to start up; damaged OCC cable or connector; faulty encoder in the 1FK2 motor; encoder interface in the converter faulty.
checks: Read the other encoder messages in the list; reseat or swap the OCC cable; try the motor on a known-good converter if one is available.
repairable: Yes: encoder replacement on the motor or repair of the converter's encoder interface.
service: Encoder repair; servo motor repair; servo drive repair

name: Drive: Motor overcurrent
meaning: The motor current went above the limit allowed for this motor, so the S210 switched it off.
symptoms: Trips when the axis accelerates, hits a load, or as soon as it is enabled.
causes: Load too high or axis jammed; short circuit or ground fault in the motor or OCC cable; current limit or control settings wrong; motor and converter not a matching pair.
checks: Check the axis moves freely; megger the motor and cable with power off; confirm the motor model matches the converter it is paired with.
repairable: Yes, when the motor winding, cable or converter output stage is damaged.
service: Servo motor repair; servo drive repair

Drive: Motor blocked/speed controller at its limit
meaning: The motor stayed at its torque limit while barely turning, so the S210 decided it is blocked.
symptoms: The axis doesn't move when commanded, then trips after a fraction of a second.
causes: Holding brake not releasing; mechanical jam; encoder fault or wrong commutation; one motor phase missing; speed loop oscillating.
checks: Listen for the brake releasing on enable; with power off, check the axis turns freely; check the motor connector and OCC cable.
repairable: Yes: brake and encoder repairs on the motor are common causes.
service: Servo motor repair; brake repair; encoder repair

name: Drive: Motor overspeed
Drive: Brake control error
meaning: The S210's built-in brake control found a fault in the circuit that opens and closes the motor's holding brake, and switched off torque for safety.
symptoms: Trips when the drive tries to open or close the brake, often on enable or stop.
causes: Broken brake wires or damaged OCC cable; cable shield not connected properly; short or ground fault in the brake coil; fault in the converter's brake output.
checks: Inspect the OCC cable and its connectors at both ends; with power off, measure the brake coil resistance and check for a short to ground.
repairable: Yes: brake coil replacement on the motor or repair of the converter's brake output.
service: Brake repair; servo motor repair; servo drive repair

Drive: overcurrent
meaning: The S210 measured more current in its output stage than the hardware allows and switched the motor off to protect the power transistors (IGBTs).
symptoms: Trips as soon as the axis is enabled, while accelerating, or at random under heavy load.
causes: Short circuit or ground fault in the motor or its OCC cable; wrong motor data or over-tuned control settings; motor rated for much more current than the converter; failed IGBTs or current sensing inside the converter; supply phase missing.
checks: With the converter isolated and the DC link discharged, megger the motor and cable phase to ground and compare the three winding resistances; check the cable is fully seated; if motor and cable test good, the converter is the likely cause.
repairable: Yes: power stage faults (IGBT, gate drive, current sensing) are a common converter repair.
service: Servo drive repair; servo motor repair

name: Drive: DC link overvoltage
meaning: The DC link (DC bus) voltage inside the S210 rose above its trip level, usually because a braking motor fed energy back faster than the converter could get rid of it.
symptoms: Trips while the axis is slowing down, on fast stops, or while a vertical axis is lowered.
causes: Deceleration too fast for the load; braking resistor missing, undersized or open; supply voltage too high or spiking; a supply phase interrupted.
checks: Note whether it always trips during braking; check the braking resistor (internal or external) and its wiring; measure the incoming line voltage.
repairable: Often a setting or braking-resistor issue; repairable when the converter's braking circuit or voltage measurement has failed.

name: Drive: DC link undervoltage
meaning: The DC link voltage dropped below the minimum the S210 needs to keep the motor running.
symptoms: Trips on supply dips, at switch-on, or when the machine draws a lot of power at once.
causes: Supply failure, voltage dip or missing phase; blown fuse; supply voltage set wrongly in the converter (1 AC vs 3 AC, 200 V vs 400 V); weak precharge circuit or DC link capacitors.
checks: Measure all supply phases under load; check fuses and terminals; confirm the line voltage setting matches the real supply.
repairable: Yes, when the converter's precharge or DC link is the cause.

name: Power unit: Overtemperature heat sink AC inverter
meaning: The S210's heat sink got hotter than its limit, so the converter shut down to protect its power stage.
symptoms: Trips after running for a while, more often on hot days or under heavy duty cycles.
causes: Cooling fan failed or blocked (3 AC units have a fan); dust on the heat sink; cabinet too hot or not enough space around the converter; overload; switching frequency set too high.
checks: Check the fan turns and the airflow path is clear; clean the heat sink; measure the cabinet temperature; compare motor current with the converter rating.
repairable: Yes: fan replacement and cleaning are simple repairs; repeated overheating can also damage the power stage.

name: Power unit: Overload I2t
meaning: The converter's thermal model calculated that it carried too much current for too long (I²t overload).
symptoms: Trips during long, heavy cycles; clears after a rest and then comes back.
causes: Mechanical binding in the axis; holding brake dragging; converter too small for the duty cycle; poorly tuned or oscillating control loop; motor fault drawing extra current.
checks: Compare the actual current with the converter rating; with power off and the axis secured, feel for binding; confirm the brake releases fully.
repairable: Often mechanical; repairable when the converter's current measurement or the motor is faulty.
service: Servo drive repair; servo motor repair

name: Power unit: Line phase failure in main circuit
meaning: The S210 saw too much ripple on its DC link voltage, which usually means one supply phase is missing or weak.
symptoms: Trips under load, especially on 3 AC units; may come and go with the plant supply.
causes: Blown fuse or loose connection on one phase; unbalanced supply; a motor phase lost; too much power drawn on a single-phase supply.
checks: Check every supply fuse and terminal; measure all three phases under load; check the motor cable connections.
repairable: Usually a supply issue; repairable when the converter's input stage or DC link is damaged.
